mainTopic: Which days need extra 'reinforcement' (חיזוק) against fasting, and was מגילת תענית cancelled after the חורבן?
overview: מגילת תענית lists the third of תשרי as a day when fasting is forbidden, and the גמרא asks why that listing was needed. In בית המקדש times, the day גדליה בן אחיקם was killed (also the third of תשרי) was already a day of joy. רב answers that the listing was needed to forbid fasting on the day before, the second of תשרי. The גמרא then asks why that day is not already forbidden, either as the day after ראש חודש or as the day before גדליה's day. The answer is a key rule, backed by a ברייתא. Torah days (and, says רב אשי, days from the Prophets, דברי קבלה) need no protective 'fence' on the days around them. Rabbinic days like those in מגילת תענית do need one. Next, רב טובי בר מתנה challenges the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled. He quotes its 28th of אדר holiday, which was added when יהודה בן שמוע and his colleagues got a Roman decree against Torah, ברית מילה and שבת cancelled. The suggestion that this happened in בית המקדש times is rejected, because יהודה בן שמוע was a student of רבי מאיר, who lived after the חורבן. A משנה about repaired glass vessels is quoted to prove this, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why list the third of תשרי if it is already גדליה's day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need for מגילת תענית to list the third of תשרי, since that day is already the day גדליה בן אחיקם was killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But derive it from the fact that it is the day on which גדליה בן אחיקם was killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why מגילת תענית had to forbid fasting on the third of תשרי. In בית המקדש times, that day was already a day of joy because it is the date of גדליה's fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא taught that when the בית המקדש stood, the fast days became days of joy. So the third of תשרי (צום גדליה) would already be a day when fasting is forbidden. If so, the listing in מגילת תענית looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it' — why not learn this law from a different, already-existing reason?
The Jewish governor whose murder is mourned on צום גדליה, the third of תשרי
An ancient list of festive days on which fasting was forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get confused by the idea that a fast day forbids fasting. The point is that in בית המקדש times, the fast days were turned into days of joy, so fasting on them was forbidden.

phrases.english: But derive it [instead]
phrases.notes: A standard challenge: the law is already known from another source.

phrases.english: from the fact that it is the day on which was killed
Gedaliah son of Ahikam!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹם שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג בּוֹ גְּדַלְיָה בֶּן אֲחִיקָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the listing of the third of תשרי in מגילת תענית, which was quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for מגילת תענית to list the third of תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The day is already a day of joy because of צום גדליה in בית המקדש times, so a separate listing adds nothing.

steps.title: The listing was needed to forbid fasting on the day before
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the listing in מגילת תענית was needed to forbid fasting on the day before, the second of תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It was needed only to forbid the day before it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that the real purpose of the listing was the day before, the second of תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Days listed in מגילת תענית also forbid fasting on the day before and the day after. So even though the third of תשרי was already forbidden, listing it added a new law: no fasting on the second of תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was needed only for…' — introduces the real purpose of a seemingly extra law

phrases.english: Rav said:
It was not needed except
to forbid [fasting on] the day before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לֶאֱסוֹר אֶת שֶׁלְּפָנָיו
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the listing has a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing the third of תשרי was pointless, since it was already a day of joy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listing was needed to extend the no-fasting rule to the second of תשרי.

steps.title: The day before is already the day after ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the second of תשרי is already the day after ראש חודש, so fasting should already be forbidden on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The day before as well: derive it from the fact that it is the day after ראש חודש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's answer. The second of תשרי seems to be already protected, because it comes right after ראש חודש (the first of תשרי).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that every festive day also forbids fasting on the days around it. If that were true, the second of תשרי would already be forbidden, and the listing would again be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Moon, the first day of the month

phrases.english: The day before it also — derive it
from the fact that it is the day
after Rosh Chodesh!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלְּפָנָיו נָמֵי, תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחַר רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the listing was needed for the day before
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second of תשרי is already next to a festive day (ראש חודש), so it should already be forbidden.

steps.title: Torah-level days do not need reinforcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ראש חודש is from the Torah, and Torah days do not need a protective rule on the days around them.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראש חודש is from the Torah, and a Torah law does not need reinforcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ראש חודש does not forbid fasting on the day after it, because it is a Torah-level day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra 'day before and day after' rule is a fence, meant to strengthen weaker rabbinic days. Torah days are strong enough on their own, so no fence was made around them. That is why the second of תשרי is not already forbidden because of ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Reinforcement; a protective extension of a law

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that only rabbinic laws need חיזוק, is the key to the rest of the sugya.

phrases.english: Rosh Chodesh is from the Torah,
and a Torah law does not need reinforcement.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וּדְאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא בָּעֵי חִיזּוּק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every festive day also forbids fasting on the days next to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only rabbinic festive days extend to the days next to them; Torah days like ראש חודש do not.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the difference between מגילת תענית days and שבת or יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the days in מגילת תענית forbid fasting on the days before and after them, but שבת and יום טוב do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: These days written in מגילת תענית are forbidden, both before them and after them. שבתות and ימים טובים are themselves forbidden, but the days before them and after them are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the principle it just stated. It begins by quoting the ברייתא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly treats the two kinds of days differently. The days of מגילת תענית extend to the neighboring days, while שבת and יום טוב do not. This matches the answer given about ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it is taught' — introduces a supporting ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught [in a baraita]:
These days that are written in Megillat Ta'anit
are forbidden [for fasting], both before them and after them.
Shabbatot and Festivals — they themselves are forbidden,
[but] before them and after them is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַיָּמִים הָאֵלֶּה הַכְּתוּבִין בִּמְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the principle of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that Torah days do not need חיזוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting the days of מגילת תענית with שבת and יום טוב

steps.title: The ברייתא asks what the difference is
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the two kinds of days are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and that?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is asked to set up the explanation. This step prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds surprising: the holier days (שבת and יום טוב) get less protection. The question invites the reason for this.

phrases.english: What is the difference between this and that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the days of מגילת תענית extend to the neighboring days but שבת and יום טוב do not

steps.title: Torah laws need no reinforcement; rabbinic laws do
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that שבת and יום טוב are from the Torah and need no חיזוק, while the days of מגילת תענית are דברי סופרים and need חיזוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are Torah laws, and Torah laws do not need reinforcement. Those are rabbinic laws, and rabbinic laws need reinforcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains that the difference depends on whether the day is from the Torah or from the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People take Torah days seriously anyway, so they need no extra fence. Rabbinic days could be taken lightly, so the Rabbis added the neighboring days to strengthen them. This is exactly the rule the גמרא used about ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: These (here: one group of days … the other group)

steps.whatToRemember: Torah-level festive days (שבת, יום טוב, ראש חודש) forbid fasting only on the day itself. Rabbinic days in מגילת תענית also forbid fasting on the day before and the day after, as חיזוק.
steps.confusionAlert: The first הַלָּלוּ refers to שבת and יום טוב (Torah), and the second refers to the days of מגילת תענית (rabbinic). Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: These [Shabbat and Festivals] are Torah law,
and Torah laws do not need reinforcement.
Those [Megillat Ta'anit days] are rabbinic law,
and rabbinic laws need reinforcement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְאֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה צְרִיכִין חִיזּוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 and confirms the principle of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Torah days do not need חיזוק; rabbinic days do.

steps.title: The second of תשרי is already the day before גדליה's day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the second of תשרי is the day before צום גדליה, so it should already be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But derive it from the fact that it is the day before the day on which גדליה בן אחיקם was killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב. The second of תשרי is right before the day of גדליה, which was a joyous day in בית המקדש times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צום גדליה is not written in the Torah. So it might seem to be like a rabbinic day that needs חיזוק, which would forbid fasting on the day before it. If so, listing the third of תשרי in מגילת תענית is again unnecessary.

phrases.english: But derive it from the fact that it is
the day before the day on which was killed
Gedaliah son of Ahikam!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹם שֶׁלִּפְנֵי יוֹם שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג בּוֹ גְּדַלְיָה בֶּן אֲחִיקָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to challenging רב's answer (step 2) after the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the listing was needed for the second of תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צום גדליה is not a Torah day, so it should need חיזוק and already forbid fasting on the day before.

steps.title: Prophetic tradition is treated like Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that צום גדליה comes from דברי קבלה (the Prophets), which are treated like Torah law and need no חיזוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: גדליה בן אחיקם is from דברי קבלה, and דברי קבלה are like Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that the day of גדליה does not forbid fasting on the day before it, because it is based on the Prophets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fasts, including צום גדליה, are mentioned in the book of זכריה. Laws from the Prophets (דברי קבלה) are strong like Torah laws, so they need no חיזוק. That leaves the listing in מגילת תענית as the only reason the second of תשרי is forbidden, and so רב's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Texts of tradition: the Prophets and Writings (נביאים וכתובים)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels: Torah law and דברי קבלה need no חיזוק, but דברי סופרים (like מגילת תענית) do. So the only source forbidding fasting on the second of תשרי is the listing of the third of תשרי in מגילת תענית, just as רב said.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּדַלְיָה בֶּן אֲחִיקָם דִּבְרֵי קַבָּלָה הוּא,
phrases.english: [The day of] Gedaliah son of Ahikam is from the texts of tradition,
and the texts of tradition are like Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: גְּדַלְיָה בֶּן אֲחִיקָם דִּבְרֵי קַבָּלָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by applying the principle of steps 4 and 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places צום גדליה in the Torah-level group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צום גדליה is not in the Torah, so it is rabbinic and needs חיזוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: דברי קבלה are treated like Torah law, so צום גדליה needs no חיזוק, and רב's explanation holds.

steps.title: רב טובי בר מתנה quotes the 28th of אדר entry
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי בר מתנה opens an objection by quoting a line from מגילת תענית about good news on the 28th of אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר מתנה raised an objection: On the twenty-eighth of אדר, good news came to the Jews that they would not have to turn away from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins here. רב טובי בר מתנה quotes an entry from מגילת תענית, and this sets up the story and the question that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מתיב tells us this is an objection to the view that מגילת תענית is cancelled. He quotes this particular date because its story will show something about when it was added. The actual attack comes in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: raised an objection (usually from a written source)

phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Mattana raised an objection:
On the twenty-eighth of it [Adar]
phrases.notes: "Of it" refers to the month of אדר in מגילת תענית.

phrases.english: good news came to the Jews
that they should not turn away from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a fresh objection to the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled. It comes after the צום גדליה discussion ended with רב אשי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that בטלה מגילת תענית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the source. The logic of the attack is spelled out in step 13.

steps.title: The Roman decree and the visit to the matron
steps.stepSummary: The story behind the holiday: Rome banned Torah study, ברית מילה and keeping שבת, so יהודה בן שמוע and his colleagues went to an influential Roman woman for advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wicked kingdom passed a decree that the Jews may not study Torah, may not circumcise their sons, and must break שבת. What did יהודה בן שמוע and his friends do? They went to ask advice from a certain noblewoman whom all the important men of Rome used to visit.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted source explains the background of the 28th of אדר holiday. It tells us what the decree was and who acted against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the name יהודה בן שמוע. It will matter later (steps 15-16), because it tells us when this story happened. The rest of the story builds toward the decree being cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who led the effort against the decree

phrases.english: For the wicked kingdom issued a decree
that they should not occupy themselves with Torah,
and that they should not circumcise their sons,
and that they should desecrate Shabbatot.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה יְהוּדָה בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ וַחֲבֵירָיו?
phrases.english: What did Yehuda ben Shammua and his colleagues do?
They went and took advice from a certain matron
whom all the great men of Rome would regularly visit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted source. It explains the background to the good news mentioned in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The story behind the 28th of אדר holiday

steps.title: The night protest and the new holiday
steps.stepSummary: Following the matron's advice, they cried out at night. The decrees were cancelled, and the day was made a יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: She told them: Come and protest loudly at night. They went and protested at night, saying: Oh Heavens! Are we not your brothers? Are we not children of one father? Are we not children of one mother? Why are we different from every other nation and language, that you make such harsh decrees against us? And the decrees were cancelled, and that day was made a holiday.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with its key fact: a new holiday was added to מגילת תענית because the decree was cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last line, that they made that day a יום טוב, is what the challenge needs. It shows the list of holidays was still growing at the time of this story.

phrases.english: She said to them: Come and cry out at night.
They went and cried out at night, saying:
O Heavens!
phrases.notes: Addressed to the Roman authorities, as if to say "you who are in the heights."

phrases.english: Are we not your brothers,
and are we not children of one father,
and are we not children of one mother?
How are we different from every nation and tongue
that you issue harsh decrees against us?
And they annulled them.
And that day they made a festive day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and gives the result: the decree was cancelled and a new holiday was set.
steps.raayaObject: That a new day was added to מגילת תענית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the story: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֲשָׂאוּהוּ יוֹם טוֹב

steps.title: Old days cancelled while new ones are added?
steps.stepSummary: If מגילת תענית was cancelled, it makes no sense that the old holidays were dropped while new ones were being added.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that מגילת תענית was cancelled, would they cancel the earlier days and add new ones later?!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual punch of רב טובי בר מתנה's objection. The story proves new holidays were still being added, so how could the whole list have been cancelled?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a new day shows the list was still in force at that time. It is unreasonable that the first days were dropped while later ones were added. So מגילת תענית should not be considered cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: and if it enters your mind (if you think)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that Megillat Ta'anit was nullified —
the first ones they annulled,
and later ones they add?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ בָּטְלָה מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story's ending (a new holiday) to attack the view that the list was cancelled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that מגילת תענית was cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A holiday was added to the list, which shows the list was still active. Cancelling the old days while adding new ones would contradict itself.

steps.title: Maybe this holiday also dates from Temple times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible defense: maybe this story also happened while the בית המקדש stood, before the list was cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too it was at the time when the Temple was standing —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible answer for the view that the list was cancelled. It immediately sets up the rejection that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that all of מגילת תענית, including this day, was in force only while the בית המקדש stood. If so, adding a day back then fits with the list being cancelled after the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you say (introduces a suggested answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. The phrase וְכִי תֵּימָא introduces an answer someone might give, and the גמרא knocks it down right away.

phrases.english: And if you say that here too
it was at the time the Temple was standing —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the event in time: the new holiday was added before the list was cancelled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The holiday was added during בית המקדש times, when מגילת תענית was still in force.
steps.terutzMaskana: This answer is rejected in step 15.

steps.title: יהודה בן שמוע lived after the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The suggested answer fails, because יהודה בן שמוע was a student of רבי מאיר, who lived after the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But יהודה בן שמוע was a student of רבי מאיר, and רבי מאיר lived after that [after the destruction]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from step 14 by dating the people in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lived after the בית המקדש was destroyed, and his student lived even later. So this holiday was added after the חורבן. That brings back the question of how the list could have been cancelled while new days were still being added.

phrases.english: But Yehuda ben Shammua
was a student of Rabbi Meir,
and Rabbi Meir lived after that [the destruction]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא יְהוּדָה בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 14, so the קשיא of step 13 is back.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the 28th of אדר holiday was added during בית המקדש times

steps.title: Proof from the glass vessels משנה
steps.stepSummary: To prove that יהודה בן שמוע was רבי מאיר's student, the גמרא quotes a משנה where he reports a ruling in רבי מאיר's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Glass vessels that got holes, and lead was dripped into them to fill the holes — רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: יהודה בן שמוע rules them impure in the name of רבי מאיר,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its claim that יהודה בן שמוע learned from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of the משנה, whether repaired glass can become impure, does not matter here. What matters is the phrase "in the name of רבי מאיר," which shows יהודה בן שמוע passed on his teacher's rulings. The quote continues on the next amud.
